title: Canonical Order
description: The canonical order model. Owned by the course, not by any assignment. From PA4 onward, every assignment reads or writes exactly this shape — do not add, rename or retype a field, even if your source system makes that convenient. There is deliberately no field for payment/card/IBAN details: a source that carries one gets it stripped during transformation (content filter pattern).

orderId.description: The order id as given by the source system. Not renumbered.

orderType.description: The business order type. One-to-one with source in this course's fixtures, but modelled separately because a future source could carry a different orderType than its channel implies.

source.description: Which translator produced this record. Provenance, not a business field.

receivedAt.description: When the canonical translator produced this record (its own clock), not the order's own timestamp. Excluded from cross-source structural comparisons for that reason.

orderDate.description: The order's own timestamp, normalized to ISO-8601 UTC regardless of the source's original representation (string, or Unix epoch seconds).

productId.description: Normalized to the pricing API's own format before enrichment. See each translator for its source-specific normalization rule.

unitPrice.description: A decimal STRING with exactly two fraction digits, e.g. "24.99". NEVER a JSON number — a float silently loses trailing zeros and, eventually, cents. Comes from the pricing API's response, not from the source order (which does not carry a trustworthy price).

currency.description: The currency the unitPrice is denominated in, as returned by the pricing API. May differ from the order-level currency below.

taxRate.description: Fraction, e.g. 0.21 for 21%. Not a monetary amount, so a number is fine here.

currency.description: The order-level currency, as declared by the source (after mapping, e.g. ISO 4217 numeric -> alpha).
